round_A_gpu_exact_seed_average.what: EXP409AVG = average of 9 seeds of the exact PLAIN w409 backbone (93, 2718, 3141, 4242, 5150, 6060, 7070, 8080, 9090)
round_A_gpu_exact_seed_average.why: Every AVG_ base we own is built from the OLD architecture. On the same fold the exact backbone is much stronger per model: exw409_s93 = 1.667960 against tcn409 = 1.674067. We have never built a multi-seed average of the strong architecture, only single seeds of it (102_probe_w409c, 127 decay).

reading_key.admission_gate: incremental gain beyond the admitted pool {w409c, decay_s93} >= 0.00008, positive_fraction >= 0.90, negative weight fraction <= 0.10
reading_key.caveat_recorded_in_advance: The measured between-seed correlation in the OLD family was 0.9968, leaving only +0.00038 correlation from 3 seeds to infinity. If the exact family behaves the same, this round is expected to FAIL its admission gate. It is run because the exact family is a stronger and never-averaged architecture, not because averaging itself is expected to be worth much.

round_B_cpu_gbdt_factorial.what: Decompose the scaled GBDT into single-factor cells against the measured control
round_B_cpu_gbdt_factorial.control_recipe: 14 anchors stride 12, learning_rate 0.05, 250 rounds, 127 leaves, 2 seeds

cells.gbdtG2_lr: learning_rate 0.05 -> 0.02 with 1500 rounds, everything else at control
cells.gbdtscale: all four factors together, already running

round_B_cpu_gbdt_factorial.why: The scaled run changes four factors at once. That is the same confound that invalidated the morning TCN density test, and it would leave a win unattributable and a loss uninformative. The decomposition is queued behind the scaled run so it never competes for cores.

reading_key.admission_still_requires: anchor-408 prediction, incremental >= 0.00008 beyond the admitted pool, then a public gate built with --expect-baseline 1.6461788499434364
